# `attachment` commands

## `attachment add`

Upload verified bytes and link them to a company record.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | attachment |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/transfers/attachment.add` |
| External binary body | input |

### CLI

`bookflow attachment add customer 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV receipt.pdf --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --caption "Service receipt" --reason "File service receipt" --json`

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `caption` | `--caption` | string | no | no | "" | Association caption, at most 2048 UTF-8 bytes.; maximum length 2048 |
| `record_type` | `RECORD_TYPE` | string | yes | no | — | Canonical annotation type, e.g. customer, account, or company_info.; minimum length 1; maximum length 64 |
| `record_id` | `RECORD_ID` | string | yes | no | — | Stable id of the target inside the selected company.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |
| `original_filename` | `--original-filename` | string | yes | no | — | Basename only, at most 255 UTF-8 bytes.; minimum length 1; maximum length 255; Required in JSON/Python; CLI defaults to PATH basename |
| `media_type` | `--media-type` | string | no | no | "application/octet-stream" | ASCII type/subtype media type.; maximum length 127; CLI guesses MIME type from PATH unless explicitly supplied |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `PATH` | Required input file on the calling machine. Original filename defaults to its basename; media type defaults to the guessed MIME type, or application/octet-stream. Explicit metadata options override these defaults. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--idempotency-key TEXT` | Retry-safe key for this create command. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### External binary body

The registry declares one `input` body separately from the JSON input and output models.

Python: pass a caller-owned binary source as `input_stream=` to `client.run('attachment add', input, ...)` or the named command method. Paths and stream objects are never command JSON fields. The return value is typed JSON metadata.

JSON requires `original_filename`; the CLI supplies its PATH basename when omitted. Python and HTTP default `media_type` to `application/octet-stream`. `--original-filename` and `--media-type` override CLI inference.

See [binary transfers](../transfers.md) for executable file examples, HTTP encoding, limits, dry runs, and local completion verification.

## `attachment list`

Page active file associations for a record, newest occurrence first.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | read |
| Required role | member |
| Capability | attachment |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/attachment.list` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow attachment list customer 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --limit 25 --json`

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `record_type` | `RECORD_TYPE` | string | yes | no | — | Canonical annotation type, e.g. customer, account, or company_info.; minimum length 1; maximum length 64 |
| `record_id` | `RECORD_ID` | string | yes | no | — | Stable id of the target inside the selected company.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |
| `limit` | `--limit` | integer | no | no | 50 | minimum 1; maximum 200 |
| `cursor` | `--cursor` | string \| null | no | yes | null | — |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/attachment.list`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |

### Output

## `attachment unlink`

Unlink an occurrence with its expected version, retaining history and bytes.

A dry run previews the proposed result without saving it. Any proposed record IDs or posted status in that preview describe the prospective save, not an existing saved record.

| Contract | Value |
|---|---|
| Scope | company |
| Kind | write |
| Required role | standard |
| Capability | attachment |
| Feature | — |
| HTTP | `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/attachment.unlink` |
| External binary body | none |

### CLI

`bookflow attachment unlink 01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV --expected-version 1 --company "Demo Plumbing Co" --reason "Remove association" --json`

### Input

| JSON field | CLI input | Type | Required | Nullable | Default | Description and constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `link` | `LINK` | string | yes | no | — | Stable link occurrence id.; minimum length 1; maximum length 26 |
| `expected_version` | `--expected-version` | integer | yes | no | — | Current link version; checked even for inactive links.; minimum 1 |

### Command and context options

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Print one JSON object. |
| `--data-root TEXT` | Data root; otherwise `BOOKFLOW_DATA_ROOT`, then `~/.bookflow`. |
| `--dry-run` | Validate and preview without writing. |
| `--reason TEXT` | Short reason for the write. |
| `--source-ref TEXT` | Identifier of the source that triggered the write. |
| `--interactive` | Prompt for input fields not supplied as arguments or options. |
| `--directive TEXT` | Standing-instruction code or id cited by the write. |
| `--company TEXT` | Company id, `Organization/Company`, or display name. |

### HTTP

Route: `POST /companies/{company_id}/commands/attachment.unlink`

Send the input object as JSON. Authentication may instead come from a browser session cookie.

| Header | Requirement | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | required for bearer clients | `Bearer <secret>` |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Name` | optional | Stable caller name recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Client-Version` | optional | Caller version recorded in audit |
| `X-Bookflow-Context-Encoding` | optional | percent-utf8: encode all reason, source-ref, directive, idempotency-key, client-name and client-version header values as UTF-8 percent encoding |
| `X-Bookflow-Company` | optional | If sent, must equal the company ULID in the route |
| `X-Bookflow-Reason` | conditional | Short reason; an agent or system write needs this or an active directive |
| `X-Bookflow-Source-Ref` | optional | Identifier of the source that triggered the write |
| `X-Bookflow-Directive` | conditional | Active directive code or id; alternative to reason for an agent or system write |
